pages.text: Two experiments have put quantum theory and gravity into one equation: gravity bending a neutron's phase, and a horizon glowing with quantum pairs. Both are $(thing)semiclassical$(): the quantum world on a smooth, classical spacetime.

Beyond them, spacetime itself must be quantum. One way to compute it is to sum over every way of building spacetime out of simple pieces - at random. With Semiclassical Gravity, the Monte Carlo Engine runs these $(thing)causal dynamical triangulations$(): four records of each experiment and two Metric Tensors make a $(item)Spin Foam Lattice$().
From here the road leads on to quantum gravity itself, and to the strings and singularities of the Codex's far end.
